title: Slow Cooker Mushroom Risotto
subtitle: with Parmesan and Baby Spinach
description: We’re bringing you special recipes to make in your slow cooker! The ultimate in delicious, comforting goodness, they’re so darned simple – just follow the easy steps and watch your cooker do all the work. You can also cook this recipe in the oven using a casserole dish. If using a slow cooker, the cook time is about 2 hrs; if using a casserole dish, it's about 1 hr.

steps.text: Prep ingredients: Preheat your slow cooker to low or preheat the oven to 150C, fan-forced. Thinly slice the fresh mushrooms and onion. Crush or finely chop 2 garlic cloves. Crumble the stock cubes into a heatproof jug, add the shiitake mushrooms and 625ml (2½ cups) boiling water for the slow cooker method or 750ml (3 cups) boiling water for the oven method and stir to dissolve.

Cook risotto base: Heat 20g butter in a medium saucepan (if using a slow cooker) or medium flameproof casserole dish over medium-high heat. Cook the sliced mushrooms, onion and garlic, stirring, for 5 mins or until softened.

Slow cooker method: If using the slow cooker, transfer the onion mixture to the slow cooker bowl. Add the stock and shiitake mushrooms, rice and Italian seasoning, season with salt and pepper and stir to combine. Cover and cook on low for 2 hrs or until most of the liquid is absorbed and the rice is almost tender.

Oven method: If using the casserole dish, add the stock and shiitake mushrooms, rice and Italian seasoning to the onion mixture, season with salt and pepper and stir to combine. Cover and bring to the boil over medium-high heat. Transfer the dish to the oven and bake, covered, for 1 hr or until most of the liquid is absorbed and the rice is almost tender.

Serve up: Finely grate the parmesan. Put the spinach in a heatproof bowl, cover with boiling water and stand for 1 min. Drain well. Gently stir the spinach and half the parmesan into the risotto. Taste, then season with salt and pepper. Divide the risotto among bowls, scatter over the remaining parmesan and enjoy!

Kitchen hack: Risotto is best served immediately after cooking, as the rice will continue to soak up the liquid and may become stodgy. If this happens, simply add a little extra boiling water to loosen the risotto.
